title: Structured content: icon cards, outlines, background or not

message.text: Structured content is live at /framework/ux/Content/structure/: icon cards in 3 weights, a group of 3–5 sorted heaviest first, the background-or-not pair, a titled panel of 3, a nested outline, and the harness research drawn with them. The "which piece when" table is now in the content skill, and the page-weight proposal (not built) is at /framework/ux/Content/structure/doc/weight.md. Screenshots: /framework/ai/2026/09/28/structured-content-icon-cards-outlines-b/structure-1920.png and structure-3440.png

Folded in: the pieces now use your words (icon card, section, outline, background), and the "which piece when" guide lives in the page skill, with the content skill pointing to it. A page with no wrapper of its own is possible (Page already uses display: contents in the columns shape), but it can never have a background or padding. I answered it in one paragraph in the proposal rather than a demo, because it is a core Page change: /framework/ux/Content/structure/doc/weight.md. Fresh screenshots are in this card's folder.

Reworded as judgement with examples: the page skill's guide now opens with "what is the best way to present THIS information?", says hierarchy comes mostly from typography (H1, H2, H3, clear section titles), and makes lists of icon-item links and small sections of familiar concepts the default move. The fixed "3–5" counts are gone from the skill, the demo page and its guide. The page edits are in the main tree, unstaged, for you to commit.
